approved_definition_context: ContDiff ℝ 1 f means that the real Fréchet derivative of f exists everywhere and depends continuously on the point.

For a complete real inner-product space, gradient f x is the Riesz vector of the Fréchet derivative of f at x; under the displayed differentiability hypothesis its pairing with v equals fderiv ℝ f x v.
The notation ∫ s in 0..1 denotes the oriented interval integral with respect to Lebesgue measure on the real parameter.

StrongConvexOn Set.univ m f means: for every x,y and real a,b with a>=0, b>=0 and a+b=1, f(a • x+b • y)<=a*f(x)+b*f(y)-a*b*(m/2*norm(x-y)^2). Domain convexity is automatic on univ; this definition does not itself restrict the sign of m.
EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d) is the real d-dimensional inner-product space with the l2 norm, including d=0.
